items.entity: MBB design domain 192×64: is it the modelled half or the full beam?
items.description: Sec. V-A says the design domain is 192×64, giving 12,288 pixel design variables (Eq. 11: v ∈ R^{192×64}; Sec. VI-A also cites a 12,288-dimensional space). The Fig. 2B caption calls the figure a 'Full-view' of the beam and says 'Using symmetry, only half of the domain is optimized.' The text never says whether 192×64 is the optimized half or the whole beam. If it is the whole beam, the optimized half would be 96×64, which contradicts the 12,288 count. It could also mean the whole 192×64 beam is analysed with no symmetry reduction, which contradicts 'only half is optimized'. The half-length:depth ratio is 3:1 in the first reading (whole beam 6:1). In the other two it is 1.5:1 (whole beam 3:1).
readings: 192×64 elements is the modelled symmetric half (192 along the span, 64 through the depth); full beam = 384×64 (span:depth 6:1)
192×64 is the full beam (span:depth 3:1); only a 96×64 half (6,144 elements) is modelled with a symmetry edge
192×64 full beam analysed entirely without symmetry reduction (12,288 elements), load at mid-span, supports at both bottom corners

items.entity: symmetry (mid-span cut) edge of the half model
items.description: The Fig. 2B caption only says 'Using symmetry, only half of the domain is optimized'. The text never states the boundary condition on the cut edge, or whether a symmetry edge is used in the FE model at all rather than modelling the full beam. Which half is kept (left or right) is only a mirror image and does not matter.
readings: mirror condition: u_x = 0 on every node of the mid-span edge, u_y free
no symmetry edge: full beam analysed, symmetry used only to describe/mirror the design

items.description: The Fig. 2B caption says only 'both lower corners are supported'. Whether each support is a pin or a roller is not stated anywhere in the text; it would only show in the support symbols of Fig. 2B, which is not available. Ref. [35] is cited for the setup, but its content is not given.
readings: half model: vertical roller (u_y = 0 only) at the bottom outer corner node (classic MBB)
half model: pin (u_x = u_y = 0) at the bottom outer corner node
full model: pin at one bottom corner, vertical roller at the other
full model: pins at both bottom corners

items.description: The Fig. 2B caption names only the 'lower corners'. It does not say whether the support acts on the single corner node or on a small patch of nodes along the bottom edge.
readings: single corner node
small patch of nodes along the bottom edge at the corner (e.g., 2–4 element widths)

items.description: The Fig. 2B caption says 'A downward force is applied at the center'. It does not say whether this is mid-span on the top edge (classic MBB) or the geometric centre of the beam. In the symmetric half model the load sits on the cut edge at an unspecified height. The exact point would only be visible in Fig. 2B.
readings: top edge at mid-span (top node of the symmetry edge in the half model)
geometric centre of the beam (mid-height node at mid-span / on the symmetry edge)

items.description: Neither Sec. V-A nor the Fig. 2B caption says whether the force is a single nodal force or is spread over several nodes or elements.
readings: single nodal point force
force distributed uniformly over a few adjacent top-edge nodes (e.g., 2–4 elements)

items.entity: magnitude of the downward force (and the half model's share)
items.description: No force magnitude is given anywhere, and the reported compliances (246, ≈270 median, 394, 735) have no units. With symmetry, the text also does not say whether the half model carries F or F/2, or whether the reported compliance is for the half or the full beam.
readings: F = 1 applied on the modelled half
F = 1 on the full beam, i.e., F/2 = 0.5 on the symmetric half model

items.description: Sec. V-A and Eq. 11 call V0 only a 'predefined volume fraction'. The value 0.4 is stated only for generating the training data (Sec. V-B). The transfer runs in Sec. VI-E use other values (0.5 at 96×32, 0.3 at 384×128). The value for the 192×64 benchmark (compliance 246) is never stated directly.

items.entity: Young's modulus of the solid material
items.description: Not given. Sec. V-A refers the setup and finite-element implementation to Ref. [35] without quoting values.
readings: E0 = 1 (normalized)
E0 = 2.1e11 Pa (steel-like physical value)

items.description: Not given. Material data are referred to Ref. [35] (Sec. V-A).

items.entity: material interpolation / SIMP penalization for K(v)
items.description: Eq. 11 uses K(v) with continuous densities 0 ≤ v_ij ≤ 1. The text never says how stiffness depends on density (SIMP exponent, continuation or another scheme); Sec. V-A refers this to Ref. [35].
readings: SIMP p = 3
SIMP with continuation p = 1 → 3
p = 1 (no penalization)

items.description: Eq. 11 allows v_ij = 0, so a lower stiffness bound is needed to keep K non-singular. No value is given.
readings: E_min = 1e-9·E0
E_min = 1e-3·E0

items.description: The governing PDE appears only in Fig. 2C, which is not available. The text does not say whether the model is plane stress or plane strain.
readings: plane stress (unit thickness)
plane strain

items.description: Sec. V-A mentions only 'pixel-level design variables' and says the 'finite-element implementation follow[s] the framework in Ref. [35]'. Element type and order are not stated, nor whether each pixel is exactly one FE element.
readings: 4-node bilinear square elements (Q4), one density per element
8-node serendipity (Q8) square elements, one density per element

items.entity: physical element size, domain size and thickness
items.description: The domain is given only in pixels (192×64). No physical length, element size or out-of-plane thickness is stated. These are needed to reproduce the reported compliance values.
readings: unit square elements (domain 192×64 length units), unit thickness
square elements scaled to a physical span (e.g., element size 1/192 of span) with thickness t ≠ 1

items.entity: cone density filter 'with a radius of 2'
items.description: Sec. V-A says only that a 'cone filter with a radius of 2' is applied to ṽ. It does not give the units (element widths or physical length), the exact kernel, whether weights are renormalized near edges, or how the symmetry edge is handled.
readings: r = 2 element widths, weights max(0, 2 − d) normalized by the local weight sum (88-line style)
r = 2 element widths, convolution with zero padding (no boundary renormalization)
r = 2 element widths with mirror padding at the symmetry edge
r = 2 in physical length units (number of elements covered depends on element size)

items.entity: field on which the volume equality is enforced
items.description: Eq. 11 imposes V(v) = V0 on the filtered physical density v. Eq. 12 instead enforces V(ṽ) = V0 on the field before the cone filter, through the bias b found by binary search; v is then obtained by filtering. Sec. V-C adds that 'the optimizer enforces the volume constraint strictly instead of the DeepONet'.
readings: V(v) = V0 on the filtered physical densities (Eq. 11)
V(ṽ) = V0 on the pre-filter densities via the sigmoid bias b (Eq. 12); filtered volume may differ slightly
inequality V(v) ≤ V0 on physical densities (standard OC/MMA)

items.entity: reference pixel-based optimizer, initial design and iteration budget
items.description: Sec. VI-A/VI-B compare against 'L-BFGS-based topology optimization' (NOTES at 246 is reported as a 1.6% improvement over it). No iteration count, initial design, stopping rule or parameterization is given for it. The training data come from L-BFGS with restarts from eroded designs (Sec. V-B). CMA-ES population size, iteration count and σ0 are given only for the photonic case.
readings: L-BFGS on unconstrained logits with the volume-preserving sigmoid (Eq. 12) + cone filter, uniform initial design, fixed budget of ~200 iterations
OC or MMA on element densities, uniform initial design at V0, stop when max density change < 0.01

locator: Sec. V-A, the MBB beam application (Fig. 2B)
